scenes.headline: How seven electrons settle on a sphere
scenes.sub: A machine-checked proof of the pentagonal bipyramid
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Marlo! Seven charges on a sphere settle into a pentagonal bipyramid, and ten agents wrote a proof of it.

scenes.text: Split the arrangements by their closest pair of points, and close each slice with an exact certificate the Lean kernel can verify.
scenes.mark: an exact certificate the Lean kernel can verify
scenes.say: The idea: slice the problem by the closest pair of points, and give each slice a certificate the kernel checks exactly.

scenes.title: From the closest pair to a checked certificate

steps.say: Take any seven distinct points, and find the two that are closest to opposite.
If no pair is nearly opposite, one bound settles the whole case.
If a pair is nearly opposite, cover that region with five slabs and a cap.
Each slice gets a certificate built from positive matrices and a lower bound on the energy.
The Lean kernel checks every certificate as exact integer arithmetic.

scenes.title: The energy to minimise
scenes.say: The energy is just a sum of inverse distances.

parts.say: Each pair adds one over the distance between the two points.
Sum that over all twenty-one pairs of points.

steps.say: On the left, a cap and five slabs cover the nearly-opposite region.
On the right, a single case covers everything else, with room to spare.

scenes.label: minimum energy E(P)
scenes.note: the bipyramid's energy, to ten places
scenes.say: The answer's energy is fourteen point four five, and every certificate has to beat it.

scenes.label: declarations a second kernel re-checked
scenes.say: A second, independent kernel re-checked all forty-seven thousand declarations, with no errors.

scenes.text: Six slices fall to a certificate; only the slice holding the bipyramid needs the hard argument.
scenes.mark: only the slice holding the bipyramid

scenes.say: To recap: split on the closest pair, bound each slice, and let two kernels check the whole thing.
